tasks.short: Attend team meetings and the early-years committee, bring agenda items, organise festivities and keep track of decisions and dates.

steps.what: Preschool teacher attends team meetings and the early-years committees
Preschool teacher prepares agenda items such as a new theme or a celebration
Preschool teacher organises festivities and finds parent helpers: by notes and messages today, with a shared task list and a helper sign-up form after the change
Preschool teacher checks the helper sign-up post before it goes: event, date, tasks, number of helpers and the class group
Preschool teacher posts the checked sign-up form to the class parents in the parent app
Parent signs up as a helper in the parent app
Preschool teacher searches old minutes and e-mails for decisions and dates
Team leader chairs the meeting and writes the minutes

tasks.design: Minutes and decisions are kept in one shared folder in {DOCS} and dates go straight into the team {CALENDAR}, so nobody searches mailboxes. Festivities use a shared task list and a helper sign-up form in the parent app of the student information system ({OTHER}), which the teacher checks and posts once to the class parents; parents sign up there. The meetings stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decisions lived in e-mail threads, and helpers were found note by note.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared folders, calendars and parent-app sign-up forms are standard school tools.
tasks.still_hard: Meeting time is set by the school, not by tools.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing the early-years view into school decisions.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less searching and chasing.

reach.learn: Whether sign-up forms raise parent help.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil records system includes a parent app.
Shared folders and calendars are standard school tooling.

assumptions: Boundary: from meetings to decisions found and events organised; the events themselves are outside.
Input contract: minutes filed by the team leader; dates entered by whoever agrees them; fallback is e-mail.
Team leader and parent time is outside the teacher's savings; parents' sign-up is shown in s6 at share 1. The check and post of the sign-up form keep their full time.
Meetings and agenda preparation do not change.
unknowns: Number of committees the teacher serves on.
research_questions: Do sign-up forms fill helper slots faster?

incremental.description: Preschool teacher adds agreed dates to the shared calendar.

approvals.approved_version: The helper sign-up form with event, date, tasks and number of helpers exactly as checked by the teacher in s3b, posted once to the named class group in the parent app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few parents use the sign-up form and minutes are not filed in the shared folder, so s3 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 70 (5.4); high: both used as designed (11.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check the duty rota, supervise the playground and lunch, hand children over at the end of the day, and swap duties when needed.

steps.what: Preschool teacher checks the paper rota for playground and lunch duty
Preschool teacher supervises the playground and halls during breaks
Preschool teacher supervises lunch in the classroom, the school's cafeteria moment
Preschool teacher hands children to parents or school transport at the end of the day
Preschool teacher swaps duties with colleagues by message

tasks.design: The duty rota moves into the school's shared {CALENDAR}, with a reminder on duty days and swaps made in the rota itself so everyone sees the current version. Supervising breaks, lunch and handover stays fully in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rota was a paper board, and swaps were agreed in chat messages nobody else saw.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared calendars with reminders are standard school tools.
tasks.still_hard: Supervision is presence and attention; there is nothing to automate in it.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the child alone at the edge of the playground.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes; the rota is easier to keep straight.

reach.learn: Whether self-service swaps reduce last-minute gaps.

evidence.claim: Shared calendars with reminders are standard school tooling.
Staff have consent rights on tools that can monitor them; a duty rota does not.

assumptions: Boundary: from checking duties to children handed over; transport arrangements are outside.
Input contract: rota made by the school administrator in the shared calendar; fallback is the paper board.
Supervision and handover do not change.
The swap is still agreed between colleagues.
unknowns: How many duties per week the teacher has.
research_questions: Do shared swaps reduce uncovered duties?

incremental.description: Preschool teacher records swaps in the shared rota.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the paper board stays in use next to the calendar, so checking keeps 70 and swaps keep 80 (2.3); high: the rota lives only in the shared calendar (5.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The preschool teacher keeps supervision and team work in person; rotas, minutes and helper lists move to shared tools.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who never misses a duty or a decision because the shared tools hold them.
